caption:
10 pieces of advice that made you worse, ranked by Cella

Cella ranks 10 pieces of famous productivity advice by how much worse they made her. Her to-do list has 41 items. YouTube long video, 16:9. No Short and no Reel in this package.
descripcion:
NAOS. Choose friction.

Cella ranks 10 pieces of famous productivity advice that made her worse, and probably you. A to-do list with 41 items, a focus app with a streak, a color-coded calendar, a podcast at 1.5x. Where there is a study it goes on the record; where there isn't, it is Cella's opinion. Send it to the friend who has a very organized plan.

0:00 The thing on the floor
0:49 #10 The to-do list (9:02 am)
2:07 #9 The focus app (9:49 am)
2:56 #8 The color-coded calendar, then #7 (10:20 am)
3:48 #6 The vision board (11:43 am)
4:25 #5 The productivity podcast (1:05 pm)
5:04 #4 Inbox zero (2:10 pm)
5:52 #3 Telling everyone (3:05 pm)
6:31 #2 The second brain (3:50 pm)
6:55 #1 This video (4:31 pm)
7:41 The last line (4:51 pm)

You'll recognize at least three.

What the research says (so you can check us):
To-do lists: Masicampo & Baumeister (2011). Consider it done! Plan making can eliminate the cognitive effects of unfulfilled goals. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 101(4), 667-683.
Habit streaks: Lally, van Jaarsveld, Potts & Wardle (2010). How are habits formed: Modelling habit formation in the real world. European Journal of Social Psychology, 40(6), 998-1009.
The planning fallacy: Buehler, Griffin & Ross (1994). Exploring the "planning fallacy": Why people underestimate their task completion times. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 67(3), 366-381.
Vision boards: Oettingen & Mayer (2002). The motivating function of thinking about the future: Expectations versus fantasies. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 83(5), 1198-1212.
Inbox zero: Leroy (2009). Why is it so hard to do my work? The challenge of attention residue when switching between work tasks. Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, 109(2), 168-181.
Telling everyone: Gollwitzer, Sheeran, Michalski & Seifert (2009). When intentions go public: Does social reality widen the intention-behavior gap? Psychological Science, 20(5), 612-618.
Making a plan: Gollwitzer (1999). Implementation intentions: Strong effects of simple plans. American Psychologist, 54(7), 493-503.

This is satire about habits. If getting started feels heavier than a habit, talk to someone you trust.

#productivity #procrastination #NAOS
alt: An 8-minute video in 16:9 about one Saturday, from 9:02 am to 4:51 pm. Cella, a small blocky black figure with two round white eyes and a red crown, stands in colored rooms next to a dotted box called the_thing that she never touches. Ten chapters of famous productivity advice from #10 to #1: a to-do list of 41 items read aloud at double speed, a focus app with a 212-day streak, a color-coded calendar, a silent five-second rule, a vision board, a podcast at 1.5x, inbox zero, announcing your goals, a second brain, and this video itself. Study citations appear on screen with a green ON THE RECORD stamp; a red CELLA'S OPINION stamp marks the ones without a study. At the end Cella writes one bad first sentence. The thumbnail shows Cella large with her red crown on a mint field, the words Advice that made you worse, Ranked by Cella, and a paper list with a red 41.
comentario_fijado: Which one did you try first? Be honest, we won't tell.
